title: Topic 5 - Debugging Tools
notes: Why debugging tools matter: systematic diagnosis vs. print statements; reducing trial-and-error.
The debugging cycle: reproduce bug, isolate cause, hypothesize fix, verify resolution.
GDB overview: GNU Debugger for C/C++ on Unix; works with programs compiled with -g.
Starting GDB: gdb ./a.out; running program inside with run args.
Breakpoints: break main; break file.c:42; conditional breakpoints with break if x>10.
Stepping: next (step over), step (into), finish (run until return), continue (resume).
Inspecting state: print var, display expr, info locals, info args.
Backtrace: bt shows call stack; frame n to switch context; up/down to move stack frames.
Watches: watch var; rwatch expr; awatch expr; stop when condition triggered.
Core dumps: enabling ulimit -c unlimited; loading with gdb ./a.out core.
Scripting GDB: source script.gdb; commands; define macros.
Valgrind overview: dynamic analysis tool; memcheck detects leaks/invalid memory use.
Typical Valgrind output: invalid read/write, use of uninitialized values, memory leak summary.
Other Valgrind tools: callgrind (profiling), helgrind (threads), massif (heap profiler).
ddd and IDE integrations: graphical frontends for GDB.
Logging vs. debugging: complementary roles; structured logs, asserts, and debug symbols.
Best practices: small reproducible tests, isolate modules, automate regression checks.
Course context: required for larger C projects and system programming labs.

quiz.question: Which compiler flag is necessary to make programs debuggable with GDB?
quiz.explanation: `-g` includes debug symbols in the compiled binary.

quiz.question: What does the GDB command `bt` show?
How do you set a conditional breakpoint in GDB?
Which Valgrind tool detects memory leaks and invalid memory use?
quiz.explanation: `memcheck` is the default tool for leaks and invalid memory.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of `ulimit -c unlimited`?
options: Enable core dumps of any size
quiz.explanation: Allows generation of core dump files when program crashes.
